title: Factorial ANOVA Interaction Detective
summary: Predict the two main effects and the interaction from a table of four cell means, then drag the means and watch the plot change.
learningObjectives: Read main effects off marginal means and explain why averaging can hide two large opposite effects.
Define an interaction as a difference of differences and show that it is unchanged by swapping the axes.
Distinguish crossover, fan and parallel patterns and say which allows a main effect to be described on its own.
Judge an interaction plot against the scale it is drawn on and the uncertainty in each cell mean.
Describe an interaction in a sentence rather than by reporting that one was significant.
interactionTypes: additive-fit button that removes the interaction
privacy: No data collected, stored or transmitted; every value is computed in the browser tab, and the tool asks nothing about the person using it.
accessibilityNotes: Native ranges, selects, radio groups and buttons, each with an explicit label and grouped in a fieldset with a legend; every cell slider announces a meaningful value such as '70.0 points for immediate feedback on the simple task'. The interaction plot is hidden from assistive technology and paired inside its figure with a visible four-column table of the cell means and both sets of marginal means; a disclosure holds the four simple effects and a paragraph showing that reading the interaction the other way round gives the same number. The two lines are told apart by dash pattern, by marker shape - circles against squares - and by a name printed at the right-hand end of each, and every point carries its value as text, so nothing depends on colour. Signed quantities are printed with an explicit plus or minus rather than relying on a trailing minus sign. The pinned primary result measures 514px tall at 1366x768 so the four cell sliders beside it stay usable above the fold. Preset, axis, uncertainty and axis-swap actions each announce a full sentence through the polite live region, focus moves to the detective heading when it opens, forced-colours rules are provided, and the layout is usable at 320px and at classroom-projector widths with no horizontal page scroll.
readmeTopic: An interaction is a difference of differences - and a plot will not tell you the scale or the uncertainty
simulationNotes: The tool holds four invented cell means for a fictional 2x2 design - feedback timing crossed with task complexity, outcome a score out of 100 - and computes row means, column means, both main effects, the interaction as (DC - DS) - (IC - IS), and the four simple effects. It deliberately reports no F, no p and no effect size, because four means carry no information about within-cell variation or sample size and an F on screen would invite a test result to be read off numbers that cannot support one. Uncertainty is instead chosen from a menu and drawn as error bars; where a standard error s is shown, the tool reports that the difference of differences carries a standard error of 2s, because four independent means each contribute s squared, and states that whether individual error bars overlap is the wrong comparison. The Remove the interaction button replaces every cell by row mean plus column mean minus grand mean, which preserves both sets of marginal means exactly and sets the interaction to zero, rounded to the slider's half-point step. Five presets occupy the shapes named in the teaching notes, including one whose interaction is half a point on a 100-point scale and looks decisive on a zoomed axis. No real study, participant, task or dataset is involved.
